text.p: First Republic Bancorp Inc, parent company of First Republic Bank, said its net income for the first quarter of 1997 was $2.0 million or $0.53 per share.
The income for the latest quarter represented an increase of $478,000 or 31 percent over the $1.5 million posted for the year-ago quarter, it said.
The higher net income was due to the bank's merger with ExecuFirst Bancorp and the resulting growth in assets over the past year, it said.

It said that after restatement to reflect the number of shares issued to Republic Bancorporation shareholders, but excluding the outstanding shares issued to ExecuFirst shareholders, the earnings per share were $0.70 for the first quarter of 1996.
The earnings per share for both periods have been adjusted to reflect the 20 percent stock stock dividend paid effective April 15, 1997, it said.

It said a major component of its earnings is the result of a tax refund program, which occurs primarily in the first quarter of every year. Earnings for the remainder of 1997 will not be significantly impacted by the program, it said.
